_what: Recorded ssh_config semantics probes for ship 007 (ssh-config-resolver).
_how: Every case below was executed against the REAL ssh binary named in _oracle, in-container, on the date in _generated. `ssh_G` is that binary's verbatim output. `resolver_effective` is what lib/sshconfig.js produces for the same input. Nothing here was written from the man page.
_why: lib/README.md, 2026-08-07: where a real implementation exists, diff against it — a maker's own oracle proves only that the code agrees with the maker.
_replay: node lib/checks/ssh-fuzz.js 1500 <seed> regenerates the RANDOM half of the evidence; this file is the hand-picked half, the surprises worth reading.

cases.what: Host matches the ORIGINAL host, never a substituted Hostname
cases.config:
Host alpha
  Hostname beta
Host beta
  Port 2222

cases.what: Match host sees the CURRENT hostname (after an earlier Hostname)
cases.config:
Host alpha
  Hostname beta
Match host beta
  Port 3333

cases.what: Match host placed BEFORE the Hostname sees the original host
cases.config:
Match host alpha
  Port 3131
Host alpha
  Hostname beta

cases.what: Match originalhost always sees the command-line host
cases.config:
Host alpha
  Hostname beta
Match originalhost alpha
  Port 4444

cases.what: Match user sees the User set earlier in the file
cases.config:
Host alpha
  User bob
Match user bob
  Port 5555

cases.what: Match user placed BEFORE the User line does NOT match
cases.config:
Match user bob
  Port 5151
Host alpha
  User bob

cases.what: A command-line user outranks every User line in the file
...and Match user keeps seeing the command-line user
cases.config:
Host *
  User cfguser
Match user cfguser
  Port 5678

cases.what: A negation-only Host list matches NOTHING
A negation vetoes wherever it sits in the list
Host pattern matching is case-SENSITIVE
...and Match host is case-INSENSITIVE
Host takes WHITESPACE-separated patterns, not commas
...while Match host takes a COMMA-separated list
First value obtained wins, across blocks
cases.config:
Host *
  User first
Host alpha
  User second

cases.what: First value obtained wins, within one block
cases.config:
Host alpha
  User one
  User two

cases.what: Directives before any Host block apply to every host
IdentityFile accumulates and replaces the defaults
Accumulators de-duplicate identical values, even non-adjacent ones
SendEnv is the accumulator that does NOT de-duplicate
RemoteCommand takes the rest of the line — a # is NOT a comment
...but an ordinary keyword does treat it as a comment
An = separator is accepted for both the block header and directives
Quoted values keep spaces; \" is an escaped quote
A # inside a token is literal
* matches empty, and crosses dots
cases.config:
Host a*b
  Port 3939
Host *
  HostKeyAlias any

cases.what: ? matches exactly one character
Default Hostname is the LOWERCASED host argument
Match all matches unconditionally
Match with two criteria is an AND
cases.config:
Match host alpha user bob
  Port 2020

cases.what: ...and fails if either criterion fails
cases.config:
Match host alpha user zed
  Port 2121

cases.what: Match canonical does not match with canonicalisation off
An unknown keyword is FATAL — ssh refuses the whole file

/tmp/orc-PaLoz6/c.cfg: terminating, 1 bad configuration options
